title: Nomenclature and description of Electro-Luminescence (EL) observations: cell cracks and other observations
mechanism: Industry nomenclature and classification proposal for EL observations (single cracks, multi-cracks, electrical-circuit anomalies, misc) tied to power-loss and safety risk.
adaptation: Defines crack-mode categories for a severity extension that can be derived from our crack + inactive masks without new labels (crack without isolation, partial isolation, isolated area).
min_experiment: No training arm; write the mask-to-crack-mode rule and report per-mode recall for all benchmark methods.
evidence: R: consensus document from the PV-Riss project, applicable to full, half and other cell formats.

alt_notes.adaptation: Map our 12 defect classes and proposed severity bands (crack mode, inactive fraction, power-loss band) onto this taxonomy so the benchmark severity labels follow a standard.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Desk mapping table, no GPU; check that each severity band is computable from our masks.

alt_notes.adaptation: Defines the crack-mode label set for a severity add-on: map predicted crack + inactive components per cell to its categories.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Severity design item: rule-based mapping of house predictions to categories on val; check agreement with an expert's coarse labels only if available.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use as the class and severity definition for the benchmark severity track and to define what non-crack dark marks (scuffs) are on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: map our 24 classes and severity bands to its categories; report severity agreement of predictions vs GT per category.

alt_notes.adaptation: Defines crack modes and severity classes for the benchmark severity track; 'miscellaneous' is the reference for non-crack dark marks such as E1 scuffs.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training arm: map our 24 classes and the scuff class onto the nomenclature and define severity labels from it.

alt_notes.adaptation: Map our 12 defect classes to the 4 categories and use them as the benchmark's severity label scheme instead of inventing one.
